methylKit is an R package for DNA methylation analysis and annotation from high-throughput bisulfite sequencing.
methylKit is designed to deal with sequencing data from RRBS and its variants.
DNA methylation in vertebrates typically occurs at CpG dinucleotides.
Non-CpG cytosines are methylated in certain tissues such as embryonic stem cells.
DNA methylation can act as an epigenetic control mechanism for gene regulation.
Methylation can hinder binding of transcription factors.
Methylated bases can be bound by methyl-binding-domain proteins which recruit chromatin remodeling factors.
Aberrant DNA methylation patterns have been associated with many human malignancies.
DNA methylation patterns can be used in a predictive manner for disease.
In malignant tissues, DNA is either hypo-methylated or hyper-methylated compared to normal tissue.
Hypo-methylation is traditionally associated with gene transcription on regulatory regions. Hyper-methylation is traditionally associated with gene repression.
In bisulfite sequencing, bisulfite converts cytosine residues to uracil but leaves 5-methylcytosine residues unaffected.
The methylation status of a base determined by high-throughput bisulfite sequencing is a percentage rather than a binary score.
The percentage of methylation determines how many of the bases aligning to a given cytosine location have actual C bases in the reads.
Sequencing errors contribute to non-binary methylation responses in high-throughput sequencing experiments.
Incomplete bisulfite conversion contributes to non-binary methylation responses.
Heterogeneity of samples and heterogeneity of paired chromosomes from the same sample contribute to non-binary methylation responses.
The methRead function returns a methylRawList object which stores methylation information per sample for each covered base.
By default methRead requires a minimum coverage of 10 reads per base.
methylKit offers methylDB classes that store methylation information in an external bgzipped file indexed by tabix.
methylDB objects include methylRawListDB, methylRawDB, methylBaseDB and methylDiffDB classes.
Most functions in methylKit work with methylDB objects the same way as with normal methylKit objects.
Bismark is a popular aligner for bisulfite sequencing reads.
The processBismarkAln function reads Bismark SAM/BAM files as methylRaw or methylRawList objects.
SAM files must be sorted by chromosome and read position columns for processBismarkAln.
BAM files should be sorted and indexed for use with processBismarkAln.
Typical percent methylation histograms should have two peaks on both ends.
In any given cell, any given base is either methylated or not.
Experiments suffering from PCR duplication bias will have a secondary peak towards the right hand side of the coverage histogram.
The unite function merges all samples for base-pair locations covered in all samples.
Setting destrand=TRUE in unite will merge reads on both strands of a CpG dinucleotide.
The default value of destrand in unite is FALSE.
Setting destrand=TRUE in unite is only advised when looking at CpG methylation.
The unite function returns a methylBase object for comparative analysis.
By default, unite produces bases/regions covered in all samples.
The min.per.group option in unite can relax the requirement for coverage in all samples.
The getCorrelation function can plot scatter plot and correlation coefficients or print a correlation matrix.
The clusterSamples function clusters samples and draws a dendrogram.
Setting plot=FALSE in clusterSamples returns a dendrogram object for manipulation.
The PCASamples function can plot a scree plot for importance of components.
The assocComp function checks which principal components are statistically associated with potential batch effects.
The assocComp function uses Kruskal-Wallis test or Wilcoxon test for categorical attributes. The assocComp function uses correlation test for numerical attributes.
The removeComp function removes principal components from methylation data.
The reconstruct function reconstructs a corrected methylBase object from a corrected percent methylation matrix.
The tileMethylCounts function tiles the genome with windows and summarizes methylation information.
The calculateDiffMeth function is the main function to calculate differential methylation.
calculateDiffMeth uses Fisher's exact test or logistic regression depending on sample size per each set.
P-values in calculateDiffMeth are adjusted to Q-values using SLIM method.
calculateDiffMeth automatically uses logistic regression when there are replicates.
The pool function can be used to pool replicates for Fisher's exact test.
The getMethylDiff function selects differentially methylated regions based on q-value and percent methylation difference cutoffs.
The overdispersion parameter in logistic regression accounts for variance greater than expected by the binomial distribution.
Overdispersion correction is not applied by default in calculateDiffMeth. The F-test is automatically used when overdispersion correction is applied in calculateDiffMeth.
Setting overdispersion="MN" applies overdispersion correction in calculateDiffMeth.
Covariates can be included in calculateDiffMeth analysis to separate their influence from treatment effect.
methylKit objects can be coerced to GRanges objects from GenomicRanges package.
The genomation package can be used to annotate differentially methylated regions with gene annotation.
